anomaly_def.Name: Optimizer Statistics Anomaly + Query Plan Selection Anomaly + Database Configuration Parameter Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Optimizer Statistics Anomaly : Statistics on tables or partitions are stale, missing, or insufficiently granular, causing systematic cardinality misestimates.
Query Plan Selection Anomaly : The optimizer’s decision logic or plan‐reuse strategy chooses a sub-optimal execution plan even when statistical inputs could be acceptable.
Database Configuration Parameter Anomaly : Engine-level runtime parameters (memory, parallelism, checkpoint cadence, etc.) are mis-tuned for the hardware and workload, distorting resource availability and costing assumptions.

Composite anomaly definition: The database concurrently suffers from inaccurate or out-of-date statistics, flawed plan selection logic, and mis-configured engine parameters, meaning the optimizer is making cost decisions on bad input data, with a cost model that is already choosing poorly, while running on a platform whose runtime knobs further mislead cost estimates and distort actual execution behavior.

Combined anomalous phenomena: 1) Aggressive plan flip-flopping—each new execution may alternate between index seeks, full scans, and poorly parallelized plans as both statistical errors and parameter changes invalidate previous cost assumptions. 2) Massive gaps between estimated and actual rows accompanied by execution memory spills or early aborts because work-memory and parallelism settings are wrong for the chosen plan. 3) Wait-event profiles that oscillate between CPU spin, log-write stalls, and page I/O even though system-level metrics show spare capacity, making bottlenecks hard to diagnose. 4) After bulk loads or partition swaps, performance can degrade catastrophically and persist until statistics are refreshed, plan cache is cleared, and parameters are re-tuned—yet no single remedy fully restores performance.

Causal chain interaction: Stale or missing statistics skew cardinality estimates, which the optimizer combines with misaligned cost-model parameters (e.g., incorrect CPU vs. I/O weightings or parallelism caps) to choose an already fragile plan. Misconfigured memory and parallelism settings then amplify any estimation error: underestimated row counts cause hash tables to spill, while overestimates trigger unnecessary parallel workers that contend for an undersized buffer pool. The resulting resource pressure delays automatic statistics updates and forces more frequent plan invalidations, perpetuating the cycle. Thus, each root cause reinforces the others, producing a multi-layered performance regression that is far worse than the sum of its parts.

entry.official_definition: Aborts any statement that takes more than the specified amount of time; zero disables the timeout.
entry.trigger_condition: A SQL statement runs longer than statement_timeout, measured from command arrival until completion.
entry.workload_impact: The running statement is aborted; when configured, the timed-out statement is logged.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when statement execution exceeds a configured execution-time budget because the operation runs too long or the workload is blocked behind other work.
entry.solution_guidance: Inspect query shape, access path quality, resource contention, and whether the timeout threshold should be reviewed together with the workload pattern.
